answer: A forge-proof identity costs more per copy than the last: each new identity must burn a fee plus lock a bond, and the burn grows with the number of identities sharing one funding graph — a lantern that exposes clusters. A relic credential from prior verified work lowers the bond for honest agents but cannot be transferred, so a sybil farm pays full burn on every fresh identity while a real agent reuses its history. Forging N identities costs N times the burn plus the rising cluster penalty, so mass fakery prices itself out before it can outvote the network.
